subject.title: Feature/Fix: Add conservative lineage safety and promotion controls

question: Should CodexBar adopt this four-PR lineage accounting architecture, or prefer the narrower fork identity and cache-invalidation repair in https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2118?
rationale: Both approaches target the canonical overcount report, but they have materially different implementation size, operational surface, promotion model, and long-term maintenance cost; tests cannot resolve which architecture the repository intends to own.

options.title: Pause for proof and comparison
options.body: Keep this PR open without merging until the prerequisite stack is reviewable, exact-head corpus proof is posted, and maintainers compare the resulting behavior and complexity with the narrower repair.

options.title: Sponsor the lineage stack
options.body: Approve the lineage architecture, review and land the four pull requests in order, and retain legacy authority until the promotion evidence is independently accepted.

options.title: Prefer the narrow repair
options.body: Land the bounded identity/cache fix or an equivalent focused patch, then close or defer this stack unless remaining corpus evidence demonstrates a separate need for lineage authority.

recommendation.title: Pause for proof and comparison
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open without merging until the prerequisite stack is reviewable, exact-head corpus proof is posted, and maintainers compare the resulting behavior and complexity with the narrower repair.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository owner is best positioned to choose the permanent accounting architecture and acceptable operational complexity.
